paras: The Regulator attack on the Witherspoon house was a night assault on the home of Dave Witherspoon, a Black man, in York County, South Carolina, on Sunday, December 23, 1888. Witherspoon fired from inside and killed William J. Harten, a white attacker, and a coroner's jury found he had acted in self-defense. A Charlotte wire dispatch instead named the Black man 'Sam Harting' and said he would be lynched if caught.
Witherspoon lived 3½ miles from town on the Pinckney road with his wife, Lydia, and her two children, whose reputed father was Harten.

According to Witherspoon's testimony, Harten and another man said 'the Regulators had said' the two children must be given up before midnight. When refused, they fired two shots into the kitchen where Lydia and the children sat, and Harten threatened to put dynamite under the house. Witherspoon fired once around the door without aiming, and Harten was later found dead of a wound through the left eye.

On Monday Witherspoon reported the shooting to Trial Justice Bell, who sent him to Coroner Caldwell. The jury, which included two Black men, found Harten was shot 'from the inside of his house, and we believe, in self-defense.' Witherspoon was nonetheless jailed on the coroner's warrant, and no report of a trial, a release, or action against the second attacker was found.

The New York Sun ran the Charlotte dispatch under the headline 'A Negro Opens Fire on Regulators'. It said 'Harting' lived with a white woman he called his wife and was 'so defiant that the white women feared him', so Regulators came to order him out of the county. Giving only the Regulators' side, it reported that he killed one man, wounded others and escaped to the woods.
The local Yorkville Enquirer, by contrast, headed its report 'HOMICIDE' and printed the testimony, the post-mortem and the verdict without comment.

The accounts differ on names, the purpose of the visit, the wounded, and whether the man fled and was hunted. The local report rests on sworn inquest testimony, and the wire's 'Harting' resembles the dead man's surname, Harten.

reader.title: Regulator attack on the Witherspoon house, York County, South Carolina
bases: Both reports describe a night visit to a Black man's house in the name of the 'Regulators', in A1 to order him out of the county and in A2 to demand two children, with shots fired into the house in A2; the only death was one of the attackers (A1, A2).

No one was killed by the Regulators; the man killed was the white attacker William J. Harten, shot by the Black householder in what a coroner's jury called self-defense (A2). A1 reports only a threat that the Black man would be lynched if caught, and A2 reports no flight or manhunt; the group was a 'crowd' in A1 but two men in A2.

A Charlotte wire brief (A1) and the local Yorkville Enquirer inquest report (A2) agree on a Sunday-night Regulator visit in York County in which a Black man shot one white man dead, but disagree on names, purpose, wounded, and whether the man fled and was hunted.

accounts.label: Charlotte wire report
accounts.gist: A defiant Black man living with a white woman was warned by a crowd of Regulators to leave the county, opened fire, killed one and wounded others, and escaped to the woods, where men were hunting him to lynch him.

accounts.label: Witherspoon's testimony
accounts.gist: Harten and another man came demanding two children the Regulators said must be given up, fired into the kitchen, threatened to dynamite the house, and he fired once blindly to drive them off.

accounts.label: Coroner's jury
accounts.gist: Harten died of a gunshot fired by Witherspoon from inside his house, in self-defense.

framing.detail: The Sun ran the Charlotte brief under 'A Negro Opens Fire on Regulators', describing the man as 'defiant' and feared by white women and reporting the lynching threat without comment.
The Yorkville Enquirer headed it 'HOMICIDE' and printed the testimony, the physical evidence of shots fired into the house, and the self-defense verdict without editorial comment.

info: Sunday night, December 23, 1888 ('last night' in a Dec. 24 dispatch; 'Sunday night last' in the Dec. 26 local paper)
Dave Witherspoon's house, 3½ miles from town on the Pinckney road (A2); 'York county, on the South Carolina line' (A1)

Target: Black householder named 'Sam Harting' in the wire (A1) and Dave Witherspoon, colored, in the local paper (A2), with his wife Lydia and her two children in the house (A2). Killed: William J. Harten, white, one of the attackers (A2).

No crime was alleged before the visit; the wire said he had 'become so defiant that the white women feared him' and lived with a white woman he called his wife (A1). The local testimony says the men came to take away two children whom Harten was said to have fathered (A2).
'Regulators' (A1); Harten and another man who invoked what 'the Regulators had said' (A2)
No report of a trial, grand jury action, or release was found.
